To gain a deeper understanding of processes beyond the Standard Model, particularly those involving the scalar sector, it is crucial to study $B^0_s$-to-light-scchar hadron decays and $B^0_s$ meson lifetimes. The CMS collaboration has updated the $B^0_s$ meson lifetime and several related measurements, utilizing both semileptonic and hadronic decay channels. Employing isospin relations, semileptonic data enables more precise updates to $B^0_d$ lifetime and related measurements, resulting in the most precise determination of the ratio of $B^0_s$ to $B^0_d$ lifetimes to 0.49%. Additionally, using flavor specific decays for the first time allows for a precise measurement of the $B^0_s$ mass difference, with a result of 0.87 ps$^{-1}$ that is consistent with other findings, offering a direct test of time evolution within the neutral $B^0_s$ system.

This research examines the estimation of value functions and optimal control policies in a class of stochastic control problems characterized by rough data. We offer a discrete approximation method and demonstrate its effectiveness. Furthermore, we utilize the result from the authors' related study concerning the convergence of value functions to provide an explicit framework for evaluating optimal feedback controls under discretization.

Our analysis of dipole anisotropy in cosmic ray directions divides the sky into two hemispheres based on dipole latitude and calculates the ratio of cosmic ray flux in each latitude. This ratio is then compared with existing data in each energy range. Initially, we employed a simple model of diffuse and isotropic cosmic ray backgrounds, with dipole amplitudes varying with energy, to interpret the data. If necessary, we adjusted the model by splitting it into multiple components with different dipole amplitudes. Our findings demonstrate that a single background component becomes sufficient above 4 EeV, but requires two components to adequately represent the data below this energy threshold. Consequently, we found that the dipole anisotropy amplitude varies with energy, showing a distinct transition at 4 EeV - from approximately 20% in this energy range to roughly 70% in higher energies.

A significant correlation between the centrality of collisions and the change in $R_{p p}$ as a function of centrality in heavy ion (A+A) events has been used to link the production yield in proton-proton and heavy ion collisions, based on the parton energy loss in a medium whose size and transport properties depend on the centrality. A linear relationship between the changes in $R_{p p}$ and N/A+A as a function of centrality has been proposed, with the slope providing an estimate of the proton-modified proton (p+pP) contribution to the collision. A model based on color screening in p+ p collisions has been used to calculate the centrality-dependent collision profile (E+A) for various values of p+ pP. A key implication of this model is that the collision profile for p+p collisions with minimum bias and at high $R_{p p}$ appears more central than actually is, which can mislead the interpretation of such collisions as central collisions containing a parton moving through a medium resembling that of a typical N/A+A collisions.

The equivalence between real and momentum-space formulations in noncommutative quantum mechanics is demonstrated, assuming a commuting momentum space. The resulting Fock-space formulation in terms of differential operators in the momentum space is precisely the noncommutative quantum mechanics previously defined in real space. The correspondence between the two formulations is established as their operator structures in their respective representations are isomorphic. Furthermore, the relationship with the Bellian mechanics previously studied is confirmed, demonstrating that the bellian parameter $\theta$ is merely a scaled version of the noncommutativity parameter.

The primary objective of the CECA challenge was to assess the effectiveness of using computer-aided analysis on the accuracy of predicting tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in the analysis of digitized tissue sections. The challenge was a direct continuation of the CeCAI competition and was limited to two-fold: estimating the number of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes and the difficulty level within tissue sections. The datasets for these estimates came from the CeCAI datasets, whereas the test sets were newly created and not disclosed prior to the competition. The test sets were a diverse array of images, including normal, enhanced, and distorted images. The accuracy of the predictions was evaluated against the ground truth data, whereas the difficulty level was internally validated. The best approach to address this challenge was to create a distinct predictor for each difficulty level and then classify each image into its respective difficulty level category. The winner's team, CSIS-UWM, developed three innovative methods to enhance the images, which improved the performance of their predictor. The first method involved a combination of histogram equalization and contrast limited adaptive enhancement, whereas the second involved a series of morphological operations to detect and enhance blood vessels, and the third involved color space conversion, histogram equalization, and morphological operations. All three methods were designed to improve the visual appearance of the images without altering the location of the lymphocytes. Although the images were enhanced to make them easier to interpret by human experts, it was discovered that the location of the lymphocytes in the images did

A new optical equalization technique, the joint decision-feedback equalization and maximum-likelihood sequence estimation (WDFE/MLSE) method, has been proposed for multi-wavelength systems that experience significant, time-varying channel impairments, including multi-channel phase noise, in a recent study. Due to the finite-varying nature of these errors, conventional equalizer designs, including those using the Miller algorithm, result in an excessive excess bandwidth and limited spectral efficiency. To address this limitation, a decision-feedback equalizer (DFE) with an extended feedback section that targets and eliminates large error bursts, has been designed. By limiting the impact of these short error bursts, the DFE/MLSE technique allows the system to benefit from full maximum likelihood (ML) detection, leading to significant gains in system performance. To enhance the robustness of the DFE/MLSE method, a novel, low-complexity optical equalizer module has been developed, allowing it to perform ML detection directly at the photodetector, without the need for digital processing. Analytical calculations and computer simulations have verified the validity of the proposed model, with the results showing the feasibility and potential applications of this new equalization technique in high-speed, multi-wavelength optical communication systems.

Neural network architectures that are specialized for a given hardware can enhance the performance of models while incurring the cost of being vendor-specific. In contrast, widely-used pre-trained models generally prioritize performance over energy and computational efficiency. To enable a balanced optimization for both aspects within pre-trained models, we introduce a technique for refining neural networks by adjusting their components to achieve the best efficiency-pre_performance balance. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem that targets the best trade-off between the size and efficiency of deep learning models, and we suggest a technique to resolve this problem that does not require additional parameters. Using this method, our framework efficiently optimizes dilated convolutional operations in TensorFlow neural networks, resulting in a single-source code that is publicly available for download. Moreover, our optimization method is versatile and适用于 various TensorFlow neural network models across different hardware platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. To further simplify the process of efficiency-performance balancing and provide a starting point for this type of optimization, we establish and provide an all-in-one package that includes best trade-off settings for multiple hardware platforms. Our approach and package can be evaluated and are described in the supplementary material, which is also provided in the supplementary material section.

This paper provides a comprehensive examination of Zinbiel algebras, focusing on their finite-dimensional structures and the associated lower central series and upper Loewenstein series. We investigate the relationships between these series, nilpotency, and solvability within Zinbiel algebras and Lie algebras. Furthermore, this paper establishes methods for defining and exploring nilpotency and solvability in Zinbiel algebras, offering a computational framework for comparing these properties across both Lie and Zinbiel algebras.

The quark-gluon plasma formed in heavy ion collisions exhibits distinct flow patterns, and due to its hydrodynamic behavior, fluctuations in flow numbers and particle counts can be used to evaluate the viscosity to entropy ratio. Advanced machine learning methods, specifically deep neural networks, have been trained to identify connections between flow pattern fluctuations and the corresponding ratio of viscosities. Initially formed by random superimpositions of flowing fireballs, entanglement between these fluctuations provides a significant and independent indicator of thermodynamic fluctuations, allowing detailed comparisons with correlations within flow patterns. Utilizing generative modeling to generate artificial data sets with varying thermodynamic fluctuations and viscosities, researchers have discovered that an ensemble of random forest models can accurately forecast the entanglement between flow pattern fluctuations as viscosities change, in agreement with analytical predictions. Furthermore, this capability is not limited to data derived from hydrodynamic simulations, and similar results have been found in analysis of event shape engineering at the Large Hadron Collider and during fixed target experiments.

We extend our previous research by considering (D)LE-formulas with inductive rules that rely on first-order correspondents, and demonstrate the computability of ALBA's extension to this enhanced framework. Furthermore, we establish a direct connection between this extended ALBA algorithm and an abstract inductive presentation of first-order correspondents. Additionally, we refine the conditions initially introduced by Zhang et al. in 2017 for the ALBA-diamond method to ensure the effective computability of inductive first-order correspondents for complex inductive signatures without requiring the existence of maximal atomic solutions.

We introduce a framework of four-valued logic for query answering under constraints that we find useful in practical scenarios. This framework allows the answer to a query to take on one of four values: yes, no, both both neither, enabling both positive and negative information to be conveyed, thereby providing an additional dimension of meaning beyond simply answering questions affirmatively or negating them. We demonstrate how this framework can be applied to database systems that incorporate contradictory or incomplete information, showing that it can yield positive and negative answers even in the presence of such information. Furthermore, we show that both model-theoretic and CWA-based approaches can be consistently explained within this framework, and that both can be achieved computationally using a single materialization step followed by the calculation of dual properties.

We introduce a novel linear state-space model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with exogenous covariates (TV-PARX), which can effectively capture complex nonlinear patterns and sudden changes in time series data with an integer outcome, such as financial trading activity. Utilizing the Kernel Smoothing method, we estimate and forecast the time-series' time-varying parameters and variance-covariance matrices using Generalized Least Squares, and employ the Kalman Filter to achieve optimal estimation of fixed-coefficient model errors. In contrast, the TV-PARX model develops a recursive simulation algorithm to get at the forecasting under time-varying parameters, and we compare this to alternative forecasting methods including the DLM, TV-PARX-GLS, and TV-PARX-GLS models. Our findings from synthetic data and real-world stock trade data indicate that the TV-PARX model's forecasts outperform those of the other models.

To make robot manipulations transferable with limited demonstrations, learning algorithms are being widely studied. A key learning approach involves neural descriptors that map object states to forces or image patterns. However, current descriptor field methods have limitations, such as needing extensive demonstrations across the entire configuration space or being confined to a particular category of gripper movements.

A novel approach called Neural Descriptor Fields (NDF) overcomes these limitations by utilizing a single demonstration within a restricted spatial range. By using local movement demonstrations to map 3D object poses to end-effector poses, the model can learn local movement demonstrations at new poses through local field modeling. With the assistance of a visual pose-neural network, the model can handle occluded objects and map spatial forces to 3D object poses.

A mathematical proof shows that the proposed model can theoretically map spatial forces to end-effector poses with inverse kinematics constraints.

Extensive experiments with a real robot using the Chomp planner have yielded promising results, demonstrating the model's ability to transfer local skills to new spatial domains with single-point demonstrations.

Evaluation with real-world multi-view force demonstrations has also produced positive outcomes, showing the model can transfer local skills to new pose domains with point demonstrations with the assistance of a neural view field.

These results indicate that the NDF model can transfer local skills to new pose domains with limited point demonstrations.

The SiD Detector is a comprehensive simulation model created for use in advanced simulations involving electrons, muons, and other particles at the future International Linear Collider. One key feature of the SiD Detector's design is its intricate calorimeter system, which offers outstanding jet energy resolution - less than 3% for energies above 100 GeV - achieved through a carefully crafted approach to shower containment and separation of hadronic and electromagnetic components. However, this level of precision comes with significant challenges, which have been addressed through various performance studies and optimization strategies. Here, we will discuss the calculations behind the model, its calibration methods, and its performance characteristics, including photon and jet reconstruction efficiency and resolution. Additionally, we will explore potential improvements that could be made to achieve better data acquisition speeds while maintaining high precision.

We have analyzed three regions within the globular cluster Tononzintla 2 (Ton2) in the Large Magellanic Cloud, using the VLT/UVES spectrograph, to obtain an age, metallicity and elemental spread in [Al/Fe], [O/Fe], [Si/Fe], [Mg/Fe], [Na/Fe], [Ca/Fe], [Ti/Fe], $+$[Ba/Fe]. We found the age of Ton2 to be $12.4^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$ Gyr, its metallicity $[M/H] = -0.19$ inconsistent with previous measurements, and a significant elemental spread particularly in $\alpha$-elements with $\sigma_{\alpha} = 0.27$ to $0.30$ dex. Ton2's elemental spread in $\alpha$-elements, metallicity, and elemental variations in groups with similar chemical compositions is unusual for a high-metallicity Galactic globular cluster. These findings suggest that Ton2's potential as a chemical laboratory to investigate the chemical evolution of intermediate and heavy elements in the galaxy's disk.

We have compiled the inaugural M. T. Redman scale-free analysis of the Formal Proof Archives (P4), revealing self-similar patterns in node connections. Our study reveals that node in-degrees in the archives follow a power-law distribution, whereas out-degrees do not. We also observed that in-degrees and out-degrees, when plotted on a logarithmic scale, exhibit similar patterns. The archives exhibit hierarchical structures, with the highest out-degrees found at the base nodes. Furthermore, the archives exhibit circular arrangements of nodes with radii proportional to the inverse of the in-degree. These proportions become more pronounced when plotted on a logarithmic scale.

The global structure of QCD in three dimensions can be investigated through a Camacho-Nieto diagram, using instanton physics and the strong-coupling behavior of the theory. By approximating the weak-coupling dynamics with large-N DQCD, a specific value of the complex coupling constant $z_c$ was determined for both moderate and strong coupling regimes. However, for the case where four theta angles are considered, $z_c$ moves significantly further from its unit circle value. By resolving the camacho-diagram for fundamental quark representations, the impact of varying theta-angle on baryon number symmetry breaking was found to follow an "all-or-nothing" pattern. Moreover, the diagram was used to establish the independence of the $\theta$-angle in the sign of the chiral condensate at large $N$, addressing the so-called Witten's $\theta$-vacuum ambiguity.

We investigate the connection between the replica symmetry breaking solution of the TAP free energy and the convergence of the approximate message passing for the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-synchronization model. The analysis reveals that the fixed point output distribution of the approximate message passing can be directly linked to the paramagnetic TAP free energy, while the optimal solution corresponds to the strong Rosemary breaking TAP free energy, along with its associated overlap and covariance fields. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-synchronization problem, we derive explicit formulas for the TAP variables under weak and strong breaking scenarios, which we visualize to illustrate the relationship between the algorithm's performance and the TAP solution. Initially, the algorithm outperforms the paramagnetic TAP fixed point; however, as the signal-to-noise ratio increases, it becomes trapped in a strong breaking TAP state, which represents both the optimal solution and the ground state of the system.

The Grawitz-Teubner (GT) method has been generalized and applied to create advanced metasurfaces using the sheet transition conditions (GSTCs). Although the GSTCs provide a useful approximation, they can suffer from inaccuracies, particularly when trying to accurately predict transmitted fields. To mitigate this limitation, a new variation of the Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTC-Gen) has been developed, modifying the GSTCs to better account for transmitted fields. Like the Generalized Born-Oppenheimer (GBO) approach, which refines Generalized Born-Oppenheimer (GB) method's transmitted field predictions, the GSTC-Gen method finds transmission as a separate entity rather than adding it to a reflection field calculation, thus making it applicable to a wider range of problems. Four distinct problems have been solved to validate the effectiveness of the GSTC-Gen method, demonstrating its ability to accurately model various scenarios, including normal incidence with $TE_{z}$ polarization, angle of incidence problems, and the design of passive and active metasurfaces for controlling transmitted fields.

In this research, we investigate how blowing-up techniques can be integrated into local orbital linearization proofs for systems undergoing rapid changes. By incorporating this approach, our study extends a recently developed theory, exploring its application near invariant manifolds formed during the blowing-up process. Through examples, we demonstrate how the upgraded framework can be used to prove orbital linearization and observe coexistence of both non-linearizable and linearizable behaviors within the same system.

A deep learning primitive architecture, the Extended Collective Pitch Network (eCPNN), is introduced as a potential function generator capable of accurately modeling the H3+ ion and water molecules. The eCPNN's design, based on the CPNN but with an added fully connected layer, allows it to create more complex potential functions with superior performance to the CPNN. By incorporating higher-order energy interaction terms, the eCPNN can model electronic correlations more effectively. Furthermore, we discover that certain CPNN and eCPNN structures universally represent specific mathematical inequalities, providing a more efficient method for calculating their minimum energy points, and we apply this technique to the H3+ ion. We also investigate the expressiveness and training dynamics of the CPNN and eCPNN architectures through a theoretical lens and practical experimentation, based on the insight into their energy interaction decomposition capability.

Recently, researchers using Sloan Digital Sky Survey data have identified a massive structure within the nearby universe, commonly referred to as the "Great Arc" or "Hairy Wall." By analyzing two-point correlation functions, we determined that the Arc's size significantly exceeds the horizon of correlation at a scale of approximately 1 billion parsecs in diameter, which is 2-3 times larger than the Sloan Great Wall. By examining the one-dimensional power spectrum, we found a substantial deviation (~5 times larger) from random distribution within this 1 Gpc scale. The findings suggest a striking and unprecedented structure within the nearby universe, possibly indicating a multiverse framework where multiple 'bubble' universes interact.

A new finding from wide-area photography is that it can accurately measure the change in dust over time, specifically the optical depth of the atmosphere, and this capability is independent of the equipment's precise sensitivity. Observations from three different locations, using different types of cameras, demonstrate the consistency of this method, which can accurately compare the relative clarity of the atmosphere without needing precise calibration. A unique feature of this approach is that it can detect sudden increases in the amount of dust or other particles in the atmosphere, a capability which is particularly relevant for studying atmospheric phenomena over a wide area. A significant advantage of this method is that it can be applied using different types of cameras, which can be a cost-effective way to monitor the atmosphere over a wide geographic region.

In estimating object pose in challenging scenes, a key issue lies in the ambiguous relationship between image projections and three-dimensional shapes of a scene. This issue is exacerbated when there are occlusions, object variations, or when the 3D structure is not well-defined. To address this challenge, we propose a novel approach that leverages prior projection groupings to model the object's 3D morphology and project these structures onto the 2D image for a more accurate estimation of the object's pose. This approach is unique in that it tackles pose estimation in an occlusion-aware manner, allowing for a direct, metric-scale pose estimation without relying on complex image-based regression models. We employ two primary techniques to achieve projection groupings: one produces coarse but reliable results under ideal conditions by training an attention-deficient network to identify well-defined projection boundaries; a second, learning-by-correction approach refines these groupings by learning deflection patterns from projection boundaries and occlusion masks, allowing for a more accurate and direct pose estimation. Our approach yields superior results on multiple benchmarks, including the AirPose and the HomePose datasets, where our method outperforms previous one-to-one approaches in terms of accuracy.

In this paper, we demonstrate that the inherent limitations of peridynamic
constitutive models directly determine where fractures will occur. Through both
analytical means and numerical simulations, we show that regions with altered
material properties cause the peridynamic kernel to behave inconsistently,
resulting in new cracks. By formulating this relationship as an optimization
problem, we derive a key formula connecting the peridynamic kernel structure to
the emergence of new cracks. This connection can be used to design constitutive
models that align with physical insights and achieve accurate predictions of
new crack formation. As a practical example, we formulate a novel constitutive
model that accurately predicts the crack patterns observed in the Sierpinski
gasket.

We propose G-Lasso-LV, a new model that integrates the Graphical Lasso framework by accounting for hidden variables and their interactions with observable ones, in a unified probabilistic model. This is in contrast to conventional G-Lasso models which are based on a simple Gaussian structure without consideration for latent variables. Our research shows that under certain conditions, we can accurately recover the graphical model's latent components, including their complex connections. Moreover, our model has the ability to accurately reconstruct the unobserved data distribution, providing a more comprehensive analysis than traditional Gesso models. Unlike previous methods that require multiple steps and do not consider flexible data structures, we have developed a singular, cohesive framework that supports both discrete and continuous data types, using a specific variational approximation to achieve our goals.

To evaluate and compare various numerical techniques used in conjunction with the Langevin dynamics solver, we performed a series of tests using the alanine dipeptide and benzene molecules as examples. The methods in question include deterministic integrators such as Verlet and Boris, stochastic variants like the random walk and Box-Muller, as well as hybrid options. We assessed each integrator in terms of computational efficiency, stability, ability to preserve equilibrium, and ability to reproduce potential of mean force (PMF) accurately when combined with the LS-Metropolis algorithm. Notably, the results showed that deterministic methods outperformed their stochastic counterparts in terms of efficiency and equilibrium preservation, allowing the use of larger time steps without sacrificing PMF fidelity. Ultimately, we found that deterministic methods led to substantial reductions in computational cost while maintaining accurate representations of system dynamics.

A generic, first-principles framework is established for implementing binary black hole boundaries条件 at a finite distance in asymptotically electric-gravity-space-times, applying particularly well to field adjustments within a stardust, planet-filled, or galaxy-like environment. The method allows implementation of binary black hole boundaries条件 independent of local coordinates, as long as worldlines are defined and timelike. The necessary worldline-based formalism is set up, and its advantages and limitations are explained through the use of Minkowski and Milne spacetimes, demonstrating how binary black hole orbits can be created by falling from rest at a specified distance in a starfield or planetfield environment. The method is further illustrated by showing how it can be applied to commonly used gauge adjustments, including the "moving puncture" method, and its limitations are demonstrated by its inability to account for localized field adjustments along the worldlines, which would be a desirable feature for generic implementations. The framework is believed to provide a solid basis for implementing physically meaningful initial conditions in various starfield or planetfield environments.

This research investigates the long-term behavior and exponential stability of a damped wave system situated on a star-shaped metric graph with an intricate elasticity structure, including absolute elasticity on the graph's endpoints and elasticity along the graph's edges. We demonstrate that, under specific elasticity conditions, the dynamical process becomes unstable, while other configurations lead to unsolvable cases for stability, ultimately showing that only a specific combination of point and boundary elasticity guarantees stable system dynamics.

This research Stycast 1090SI's acoustic characteristics relative to polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) are investigated. Two-part Stycast 1090SI's sound transmission loss tests demonstrate area average results -0.25dB higher than PMMA equivalents at frequencies 0.5kHz through 2.0kHz. Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations, assuming homogeneous material properties, yield results close to experimental data but also demonstrate discrepancies due to the Stycast's inhomogeneous nature. As a result, revised material properties are determined by adjusting finite layers' acoustic characteristics to match test data better.

In this study, we examine how nodes and connections function across multiple layers of a network, with a focus on networks that represent real-world scenarios, such as biomedical and social systems. We define the inter-layer topology by assessing the significance of a network node based on its position within its primary layer and any additional layers where it appears. To facilitate this analysis, we hold the total number of network nodes constant, allowing for the comparison of nodes within the same primary layer. Our analysis utilizes three distinct metrics to evaluate the structural similarity between nodes within the same layer and those across different layers. We highlight that the computation of node centrality is heavily dependent on the inter-layer topology, emphasizing the necessity of analyzing these properties. We also demonstrate the relevance of certain nodes with high centrality scores by comparing them to highly influential or central entities in each analyzed system. Furthermore, our findings suggest that certain nodes may have critical roles across multiple layers, while others may require further investigation to fully understand their multifaceted nature.

This research addresses the challenges of color-dependent point spread variations in wideband cameras, leading to color-dependent blurring in multi-color images. A novel, color-independent measurement method is proposed, based on converting image data to LAB color space and computing the lightness channel's standard deviation. The study reveals that traditional measurement methods are color-space dependent, with significant differences in measured values across different color spaces. The proposed lightness-based approach demonstrates improved clarity and consistency in representing actual color differences in camera images.

The study involves creating an analogue of the Dirac equation within the R-Minkowski spacetime, a type of spacetime with modified curvature properties. A rigorous demonstration of the solvability of this analogue is carried out using the complete set of fundamental equations defining R-Minkowski spacetime. Furthermore, it is established that the analogue is directly connected to the Dirac equation within de Sitter spacetime through a series of geometric transformations, including the conformal and unitary mappings that link the two spacetimes.

We have developed the Causal Graph Modeling package package (package Causal Graph Modeling, or 'cdt' for short) in R, a comprehensive tool for estimating parameters and constructing a graph structure in line with the assumptions made in a causal and probabilistic model. The package allows users to efficiently build and estimate a class of Bayesian Network models that include Algebraic Causal Models (ACMs), which include Gaussian graphical models as a subset. The implementation of 'cdt' was designed with a focus on usability for a wide variety of users, including those without extensive experience with probabilistic modeling. The package was written in C++ with an intuitive R interface, taking advantage of the speed benefits of the C++ backend while maintaining the usability benefits of the R language. The source code for 'cdt' is available on GitHub at the following URL: https://github.com/lorenzo-devall/causal-dgm.

A type of surface seal, known as an elastohydrodynamic contact, can develop a cavity where pressure lower than that of the ambient surroundings may trigger a sudden closure. This phenomenon was studied numerically to analyze the pressure drop's effect on the seal's behavior. To model this, an equation of state that accounts for changes in ambient ambient conditions, the seal was modeled with an elastic material constitutive equation. This model was integrated with a two-dimensional isoviscous fluid film and validated against existing data. Consequences of the pressure reduction in the cavity were illustrated, showing how the increased impact speed leads to an exponential increase in the cavity length. This table presents a quantitative relationship between the dimensionless film thickness at the leading edge and the dimensionless impact speed. Furthermore, the study found that the closure of the cavity can be divided into two phases: a gradual expansion of the cavity and a rapid closure that occurs when the expanding cavity accelerates and causes a sudden collapse. This closure can be modeled using a mathematical equation, which predicts the dimensionless time to closure as a function of the dimensionless cavity expansion time.

Using string-field theory, the F-term is calculated for both open and closed strings, as well as their combined interaction. The analysis of the general Witten effect is grounded in these findings, which provide the motivation for the study of SUSY breaking in both open and closed string theories. The resulting expressions for the F-term include contributions from both the gauge group and the cosmological constant, which are essential components of the SUSY breaking scenario. The breaking of SUSY in this planar model is represented by the cosmological constant term, while the gauge group is represented by the open string contribution. The resulting theory contains both the dilaton and the graviton, which are represented by the closed string contribution. The calculation of the Witten effect shows that charged states can be formed by combining neutral states from both the open and closed string interactions, and their masses are determined by the balance between the cosmological constant and the SUSY breaking parameters. The model proposed by Babu, Bobois, Chivashvili, and Kaloper provides a framework for realizing the KKLTT scenario, and the calculation of the Witten effect can be used to form charged states in this framework.

Mobile applications have become ubiquitous, but unfortunately, many of them suffer from various vulnerabilities. To address this challenge, a framework called OctopOS has been developed for Android application development with a focus on ensuring maximum security. OctopOS consists of multiple layers, each serving a distinct purpose, and it provides an array of security features such as input validation, code obfuscation, and anti-tampering mechanisms. As an innovative solution, OctopOS aims to elevate the security standards of mobile applications, and initial evaluations using dynamic and static techniques have demonstrated its effectiveness in resisting various attacks, including reverse engineering and runtime interference. Moreover, OctopOS has proven practical for the secure development of real-world applications, including one that was publicly scrutinized and found to be free from security issues.

We tackle the challenge of learning optimal strategies in non-limited Markov decision processes (MDPs) with unknown dynamics, where an adversary introduces inaccuracies into the simulated transitions. Our approach centers on a finite-set virtual value function approximation Monte Carlo policy learning algorithm. This method exhibits a key advantage: it has a proven learning performance guarantee (regret bound) even in scenarios where malicious data includes flawed simulation data, under specific conditions. Our analysis yields an upper bound on the cumulative loss that grows at a slower rate than the square root of the number of learning cycles when the simulation inaccuracies are fixed. Moreover, we refine a previous best-case performance bound that depends on the inverse of the differences between the largest and smallest possible outcomes. Notably, this bound is independent of the total number of decisions made during each learning cycle.

A variant of the famous paradox related to the quantum strategy in the classic "box game" has been explored, focusing on two aspects: the quantum strategy's validity and the concept of an element of choice within the quantum context. To address these concerns, a new, unified quantum framework has been established and applied to resolve the paradox and investigate elements of choice within quantum systems.

Our mean field +U calculations and experimental band structure analysis of cubanite provide a comprehensive explanation for the material's unexpected properties. Specifically, they address the following questions: why does LiF-molecularelectron spectroscopy indicate multiple bands with zero binding energy, how does the material maintain charge stability and ferromagnetic ordering despite electron spin polarization promoting antiferromagnetic ordering, and what causes a high effective mass of electrons in the valence band. Moreover, the study uses an independent variables approach to resolve the challenge of simultaneously determining chemical potential and magnetic exchange interaction, and it proposes a unique model for LiF-molecularelectron spectroscopy of cubanite.

The study combines theory and numerical data to analyze a quantum dot coupled with an acoustic cavity driven by a laser. By using a master equation approach, it shows that frequency changes in the driving laser have a significant impact on dynamics observed in intensity oscillations, providing a method for precise frequency estimation. Additionally, it reveals that the spectral response can be improved through the optimization of system parameters, and it derives an analytical expression to describe this relationship.

A comprehensive examination of the herringbone lattice Hamiltonian was undertaken, 
focusing on a general class of theories that encompass various incarnations 
characterized by distinct massless and massive Dirac points. Leveraging the 
identification of unitary transformations that preserve or introduce mass in the 
Hamiltonian, we systematically explored the effects of adding on-site terms 
related to four-fold and four-fold symmetric symmetries. This exploration 
reveals how different additions can either maintain or disrupt the lattice's 
herringbone characteristics, potentially integrating another Dirac point with 
distinct properties. Furthermore, our study maps the potential movements of 
Dirac points within the lattice's Brillouin zone, demonstrating that some 
movements can be realized through modifications to the Hamiltonian parameters. 
However, other movements, such as moving a Dirac point from the zone center to 
the boundary, cannot be achieved through this method. A mean-field theory was 
also developed to explain the emergence of magnetic flux in the lattice's 
elementary plaquettes, resulting in four-fold symmetric mass terms within the 
Hamiltonian. This development can be explained by the spontaneous breaking of 
lattice symmetries upon filling the lattice's elementary quanta of flux.

Researchers have successfully created single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) with positive photon number distributions by combining coherent and single-photon states in a lossless cavity and employing measurement-induced projection. We propose two additional generation methods: the first uses a beam splitter to mix a coherent state and single-photon state, while the second succeeds in producing SPCCSs with negative photon number districts. The second method involves a parametric amplifier that amplifies the coherent state while attenuating the single-photon state. The probability of successfully generating the target state differs in both proposals, with the probability being higher for the negative photon number cases. We show that the two models can be controlled and measured through quantum state tomography, and propose conditional operations to improve the success probabilities of the beam splitter model. As a practical application, we demonstrate that SPCCSs can effectively distinguish between two weak optical signals with high discrimination probabilities.

The Newman-Penrose formalism is a set of tools based on the geometric properties of null vectors that are well-suited for analyzing highly radiating systems in general relativity. This document provides a detailed explanation of the formalism by presenting the Newman-Penrose null tetrads in terms of the complex spinor tetrads using the Newman-Penrose formalism to derive the expressions for the complex Weyl tensor coefficients' expressions in the formalism.

Researchers have developed a new method for inferring the properties of polymers using a graph-based framework that builds on a concept of repeating units within the polymer structure. This model utilizes a hierarchical approach, applying summary transformations to connect the polymer's overall components with its individual building blocks, and extends using directed graphical models to enable efficient parameter estimation and inference. Initially developed to analyze DNA-binding properties, the model demonstrates flexibility in analyzing a diverse range of polymers, with potential applications extending beyond biological macromolecules to materials composed of well-defined repeating units.

This study introduces an innovative breathing assistance system that allows for ventilating multiple patients with one machine. The proposed concept utilizes recirculating circuits to enable two people to be supported by a single ventilator. While the designers originally intended for opposite-bed arrangement, our simulations show effective results even when patients are set up in adjacent beds. The system's performance demonstrates that they can each be ventilated with their own separate settings, including tidal volume, because the introduced losses in the additional circuits do not significantly interfere with TIV delivery. Furthermore, nearly negligible effects on TIV and positive end-expiratory pressure are observed when the ventilated patients are set up in adjacent beds. Due to the non-invasive nature of setting up the recirculating circuits, this system could potentially be implemented with relative ease in a hospital setting.

Accurate automatic segmentation of the esophagus inside the chest is crucial for non-invasive monitoring of the esophagus, a non-invasive method to monitor the esophagus can be achieved by monitoring the esophagus's luminal area. Convolutions used in deep learning models that have proven successful at segmenting other body parts may not be as effective at modeling long-range dependencies within the esophagus. To address this limitation, a novel model called Dilated Dense Attention Unet has been proposed, equipped with attention modules that allow the model to concentrate on the most relevant luminal regions of the esophagus. To further enhance its performance, a densely connected architecture has been employed, coupled with an attention-unet module to precisely segment contours. To train this model, a comprehensive dataset called EsophWeb, a collection of axial CT scans with corresponding manual annotations for luminal segmentation, has been utilized. Experimental evaluations have yielded impressive results, with the model called EsophUnet outperforming current state-of-the-art methods and achieving a Dice score of 0.937 and a Hausdorff Distance of 9.5mm. To demonstrate further utility, the model has been utilized to model the airway tree, yielding accurate results with a Dice score of 0.946.

Oil sands reservoirs, vast in size, necessitate precise and efficient analysis for optimal production. Traditional well logging, though vital, is hindered by time-consuming manual interpretation and lengthy lab tests, resulting in delayed evaluation. A novel approach, the LM-EnRML model, utilizes data from low-frequency well logging and surface seismic testing for rapid, accurate well logging interpretation. This study integrates the LSTM neural network with the Ensemble RML to create an efficient geological model that accurately predicts porosity and salt content from logging and seismic data, while significantly reducing computational time and data requirements. A case study in the Sandhill well, located in the Aquistore injection well pad, validates the method, yielding a predicted porosity of 17.6% compared to a measured value of 17.4%, and a predicted volumetric fractional saline content of 0.29 ppm compared to 0.29 ppm. The method's efficiency allows for real-time well monitoring and prediction, with an 800-fold reduction in processing time over traditional inverse methods.

Our research focuses on improving the performance of named entity recognition systems by leveraging context-rich background information from entire text corpora. We developed a new approach using BERT-based sentence encoders and BERT-based sentence sentence pair encoders, which successfully extracted general background information and enhanced the entity recognition performance of the target sentence. Our method was tested on the MSRA corpus and showed notable gains, with one model configuration surpassing the average precision and recall by 6.33 and 5.14 percentage points, respectively, when compared to the baseline. Although its total improvement might seem modest, this approach represents the first time since 2019 that a significant entity recognition breakthrough has been achieved at the CMU NLP workshop.

We employ the rationality of bitangents in the generic tropical plane curve to analyze and classify the behavior of bitangents in the tropical plane curve as it is rationalized, utilizing an equivariant approach. A specific and systematic relationship between the bitangent in the special fiber and its counterpart in the generic fiber is identified, with an equivariant construction that ensures rationality. An example is provided where the bitangent line in the special fiber cannot be directly lifted to the generic curve due to a twist in the tropicalized segment, but its equivariant counterpart does remain rational in the generic curve. An attempt is made to generalize this relationship to other tangents in a similar, if not entirely successful manner.

The paper presents a new algorithm for estimating the position of users in a mobile network that uses multiple angles of arrival and assumes a normal distribution for measurement errors. To test the algorithm, measurement data was obtained in a building and used to evaluate its effectiveness, showing that its average error is 0.89 meters, which is 325% better than the conventional method. Although the algorithm meets its design goal of a 5-meter average error, there are some cases with a 10.22-meter average error in different areas. Further research should focus on improving its accuracy in these locations.

Advances in natural language processing through deep learning have yielded significant results, but this progress is mostly visible in English. In this report, we explore the potential for NLP research to have a positive impact on multilingual societies through the development of multilingual models. We discuss the limitations of current models and the challenges that need to be overcome to address real-world needs. We also highlight key applications that multilingual NLP can serve, such as news aggregation and multilingual search, and discuss the opportunities and challenges presented by the large datasets available for processing vast amounts of data.

A significant number of people worldwide are affected by visual impairments, 
with a large portion of them depending on assistive technology, including 
screen readers, to navigate the internet. A key component of this technology is 
accessibility in web pages, which can be achieved through effective 
text-to-speech systems that convert audio input to descriptive text. Present 
screen readers typically operate on rule-based algorithms, resulting in the 
generation of descriptions that are often irrelevant or excessive. Existing 
guidelines for describing images are insufficient to produce concise and 
meaningful descriptions that are visually descriptive. Current image 
description datasets are unsuitable for this task due to their annotators' 
tendency to over-tag images with too many descriptors. User studies are crucial 
for the design of effective image description systems that enhance the user 
experience. This paper outlines the limitations of current methods and resources 
for image description and highlights the importance of user-centric design in 
this context. A user study is suggested as a necessary step to establish user 
preferences for image description.

Researchers have long studied the loss functions of tantalum oxide (TaO), a material with strong spin-orbit effects, to better understand its properties. However, previous studies that neglected the spin-orbit and local field effects, which are crucial for TaO, limited their applicability. Using a rigorous approach, this work incorporated the spin-orbit and local field effects into the computation of energy loss functions, which can serve as a benchmark for future experiments with oxide materials. The results showed distinct features, including a narrow energy loss peak at 52 eV and modifications to the low-energy peak structure, which are indicative of taubrium's identity. Nevertheless, some discrepancies between computational models and actual electron energy-loss spectra may arise from previous preparations of TaO samples.

The rapid online dissemination of unverified information poses significant challenges for society and will be a key issue for generations to come. While research has extensively explored the online propagation of fake news, little is known about the dynamics of users' interactions as they interact with and distribute false information. This study investigates the features that influence a user's exposure to and dissemination of unverified news. Data was collected from two distinct regions in Brazil with distinct geographical characteristics and political standings. By analyzing the temporal distribution of a user's exposure, we identified distinct communities with opposing political viewpoints. The data shows that the phenomenon known as 'The Big Sort' has a major impact on the online dissemination of unverified information, with users in more isolated regions experiencing greater variability in both their exposure and dissemination patterns. The phenomenon known as 'The Big Sort' also contributes significantly to unequal dissemination of unverified information within each community, with the most extreme cases often being those located in more isolated regions. In essence, the data suggests that political and geographical isolation can have a profound effect on the spread of unverified information, with the most extreme cases often being those located in more isolated regions.

We investigate how varying conditions during teaching tasks impact speech concepts. Humans instructed a robotic arm to perform tasks multiple times under different conditions. Each instruction corresponds to a distinct demonstration and carries the same underlying speech instruction, which can be seen as a consistent underlying concept. By treating each demonstration as an input and its corresponding speech instruction as an output, we built 16 separate models to compare their underlying concepts. Our research found that changes in demonstration types significantly impact the output concepts, but other variations have little impact. Additionally, we used knowledge distillation to stabilize the model and successfully used a single model for all demonstrations. These findings provide a framework for assessing and understanding changes in conceptual representations within neural networks.

Building on the successful method for reconstructing unordered trees using the NotoTree algorithm, we introduce an extension to ordered trees known as NotoOrderTree. This new algorithm follows a similar approach to its predecessor but incorporates additional considerations for outdegree order preservation. By modifying the cost function to account for this preservation, we allow for the specification of maximum outdegree values at each node in the input signal without necessitating a complete detail of the tree structure. We assess the algorithm's performance through an extended version of the visual navigation experiment, again showing enhanced tree accuracy when utilizing our cost function modifier.

The functional form of the Yang-Mills flow on the group of Lie provides a framework to study the minimization of the Casus norm under certain constraints. By parameterizing the flow via a pseudo-gradient vector field in the algebra of Lie, the continuous descent of the norm is ensured. This paper proves that the optimal solution to the given dynamical system aligns with a stationary point of the associated Euler-Arnold equations, thus connecting the two areas. Notable examples are analyzed, including the SPDE derivation for the Yang-Mills flow on the group of SU, as well as applications to minimal immersion and harmonic map solutions.

Testing and validating conversational systems is crucial, but the vast number of possible dialogues makes it necessary to rely on automated testing frameworks. These frameworks are becoming increasingly complex, necessitating their adaptability to various development and testing scenarios. However, a key issue persists: the absence of a unified standard for frameworks to address the diverse requirements of testing complex systems, particularly in the face of the numerous available options. This standard deficiency hampers the ability of the framework community to guide their design, features, and functionalities, resulting in the lack of existing survey literature that discusses their requirements and capabilities. As a initial step toward rectifying this gap, this work presents a compilation of the most prominent testing frameworks for conversational systems, as well as a compilation of their key components and features.

This research explores the use of cross-lingual memory techniques to enhance the translation performance of English to low-resource languages, focusing on the potential of a cross-lingual memory retriever to outperform traditional bilingual translation methods. A novel retrieval strategy tailored to translation tasks was developed, along with an exploration of incorporating multiple source and target language memories through a sophisticated retrieval model. Experimental results across three different language pairs were consistent in showing that the cross-lingual memory framework resulted in notable improvements in translation accuracy, with the most significant gains observed in the Vietnamese translation.

The Planck satellite's observations of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) have confirmed the overall predictions of the $\Lambda$CDM model. Nevertheless, small-area irregularities in the CMB map have been found to deviate slightly from theoretical expectations. Various researchers have searched for large-scale patterns in the CMB without much success. Some have even reported finding evidence of circular features centered near the Milky Way's anti-galactic pole. To investigate the possible impact of a nearby poloidal source on the CMB anisotropies, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the temperature map produced by Planck. In line with previous studies, we found that so-called "Hawking points" and low-variance circles are not over-represented in the northern hemisphere of the CMB map. In contrast, large clusters of hot spots are more prevalent near the anti-galactic pole. Additionally, we discovered that the absence of cold spots near this pole has a significant effect on the distribution of the $a_\ell$ multipole coefficients, making the low-variance circles more noticeable. Our results indicate that the distribution of temperature differences near 90$^\circ$ deviates significantly from a Gaussian pattern, which could suggest the local inflationary model's incompatibility with observations. This study applies the technique of subsolutions and blow-up points to analyze the dynamics of a dynamic equation, known as the Yamabe flow, on a compact, positively curved manifold. Specifically, on a star-shaped manifold, this method demonstrates that a particular initial configuration will lead to a finite time singularity. Conversely, it is shown that another, differently structured initial configuration will result in a solution with infinite time longevity. Furthermore, the work is capable of obtaining localized and semi-global solutions.

A new framework is presented that securely tackles the challenge of few-shot learning by identifying and eliminating unreliable data points. This framework, based on a contrastive projection framework (CPF), utilizes auxiliary labels from previous tasks to generate task-specific projections and distinguish reliable metadata. By contrasting the features of reliable and irrelevant data, the CPF is capable of producing high-quality prototypes. Within each task, the framework adapts its projection and classification modules through an end-to-end optimization process. Notably, the CPF introduces an innovative approach that distinguishes it from traditional methods that differentiate classification and identification. The framework's performance is further enhanced by the introduction of entropy and confidence difference criteria, which set new standards in the field of self-supervised learning. Through comprehensive experiments on the miniImageNet and few-shot classification benchmarks, the proposed framework's superiority is validated through rigorous evaluations and visualized results.

User preference is a vital component in recommendation systems, and incorporating aspect preferences within the broader preference context is a crucial step. Aspect preferences are complex and consist of multiple dimensions, such as product style, price range, and brand, which are often interconnected and embedded within user behavior data. To capture these nuances, GAE4IP proposes Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement, a novel network structure with multiple dimension modules that include the Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement (GAPE) module. Specifically, GAPE refines the explicit preference representation by integrating implicit behavioral information, using an aspect mask vector that is learned independently of user behavior. Through interactive learning, GAPE enhances the aspect preference vector, enabling more precise aspect preference representation that can be interpreted by another independent interpretation layer. Experimental evaluations on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of GAE4IP, and performance improvements over current SOTA models.

This research focuses on nature-based formulations for solving the quadratic 0-1 optimization problem, offering a simpler and more direct approach to traditional extended formulations that incorporate auxiliary variables. By utilizing exotic cones, including the exponential family of cones developed by Ben Tayeb and the elliptopolyhedral cone proposed by Katchalski, the authors derive new extended formulations with customized projection tricks. These projections enable a seamless integration with state-of-the-art solvers like SEMDEF and SDPA. Experimental results from a visualization study show that the proposed natural formulations, in many cases, perform comparably to extended formulations and can be particularly efficient for specific types of problems with inputs that resemble the generators of exotic cones.

The data composition in training sets can significantly influence how models assessed on new data perform, which is a critical consideration, yet rarely taken into account, particularly in the field of neuroimaging. In order to address this issue, we propose an approach to measure the variability in model performance evaluations. We define our method through the lens of statistical variability, which we term evaluation variability variability. Utilizing a diversity-variance matrix, we can predict unmeasured model performance variations based on unseen dataset combinations. We have applied our method to various deep learning models used in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis from MRI images. By analyzing unseen dataset combinations, we found that our method's predictions were more accurate than our measurements, validating its capability to gauge variability in performance evaluations.

We introduce a framework for network-based optimization problems involving multiple agents, where the framework allows any differentiable objective to be expressed as a network, and we propose two specialized families of objectives - Gaussian Process Regression and Convolution - that are commonly used in the research field. We develop an efficient optimization algorithm using the network framework for both types of problems, and we evaluate our algorithm through various research experiments, and we also demonstrate its flexibility by solving a super-resolution image problem and a multilingual translation benchmark problem.

Researchers have investigated the performance of various file system operations on Optane DC Persistent Memory (PMM) modules using the NOVA-relaxed file system, focusing on small write tasks. Three types of workloads were used to simulate real-world applications: database workloads, search engine workloads, and general workloads. Our findings demonstrate that the NOVA-relaxed NVMM file system significantly outperforms the operating system's combined use of Optane DC PMMs and SSDs, achieving a threefold improvement in performance. Notably, specific workloads even exhibit a tenfold performance gain with the NOVA-relaxed NVMM file system compared to Optane DC PMMs and SSDs.

Andriy Suslov's thesis explores the development of social interactions in multi-agent systems, with a focus on the motivation behind collaborative behaviors. The project builds upon the Andreas Dittmann motivated agents framework, creating an extended model that incorporates a social component. This new framework's agents learn to value cooperation and collaboration through a learning algorithm that can be applied to various collaborative behaviors, including the rendezvous behavior studied through the Andr2ySuslovRendezvousModel algorithm.

The study on the $R_xM_{1-x}M' _3$ hexagonal compounds has been guided by the success of the $RFe_5$ compounds, with a focus on achieving high magnetic moments through the incorporation of 4$d$ or 5$d$ metals.  Recent studies on the $RM_3$ compounds have demonstrated the possibility of integrating rare-earth atoms within the $M_3$ layers, maintaining $h-Pm3n$ symmetry and providing unique $R$-$M$ interactions for the investigation of rare-earth magnetism.  The present study has investigated the magnetic properties of the $R$-$Cu_3$ ($R$ = $Gd$ to $Dy$, $Tb$, $Tm$) compounds, with neutron diffraction, x-ray diffraction, and specific heat measurements performed to determine the onset of magnetism, the magnitude of the magnetic moment, and the magnitude of the rare-earth atom occupation rate.  The results demonstrate that the compounds exhibit $GdMn_2$-type magnetic moments of approximately $7.0 \mu_B$ with a linear decrease from $GdCu_3$ to $DyCu_3$ and a non-monotonic decrease from $GdCu_3$ to $TbCu_3$ to $TmCu_3$, consistent with the crystal electric field ground state.
